explanation.question_quote: On physical examination, he presents with fine rales in both lungs, his abdomen is non-distended non-tender, and there is 2+ lower limb pitting edema up to his knees.
explanation.sentence: The patient has orthopnea, bilateral rales, and pitting edema to the knees.
This combination of pulmonary and peripheral congestion points to acute decompensated heart failure.
Intravenous furosemide is the best initial treatment to relieve congestion despite the elevated creatinine.
The elevated BUN-to-creatinine ratio does not establish volume depletion, and normal saline could worsen his pulmonary congestion.
There is no evidence of shock requiring norepinephrine or of hepatorenal syndrome warranting terlipressin.
